canonical_title: Model Soups: Averaging Weights of Multiple Fine-Tuned Models Improves Accuracy Without Increasing Inference Time
authors: Mitchell Wortsman, Gabriel Ilharco, Samir Yitzhak Gadre, Rebecca Roelofs, Raphael Gontijo-Lopes, Ari S. Morcos, Hongseok Namkoong, Ali Farhadi, Yair Carmon, Simon Kornblith, Ludwig Schmidt
venue: ICML 2022 (39th International Conference on Machine Learning)

prior_identity.title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time (CORRECT)

corrected_identity.title: Model Soups: Averaging Weights of Multiple Fine-Tuned Models Improves Accuracy Without Increasing Inference Time
corrected_identity.authors: Wortsman et al. (UW, Columbia, Google Research, Meta AI, Tel Aviv University)

identity_corrections: All identity fields correct. No corrections needed.
abstract_snippet: Instead of selecting the individual fine-tuned model which achieves the highest accuracy on validation, we average the weights of multiple models fine-tuned with different hyperparameter configurations, calling the result a 'model soup.' Averaging requires no additional training and adds no cost at inference time. ViT-G model soup achieves 90.94% on ImageNet, a new SotA. Model soups improve in-distribution and out-of-distribution performance.
what_the_paper_supports: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models from same pre-trained initialization. Key insight: fine-tuned models from same initialization lie in the same loss basin, making weight averaging viable. Two variants: (1) uniform soup (average all), (2) greedy soup (sequentially add models if they improve validation accuracy). Achieves SotA on ImageNet (90.94%) with 25% fewer FLOPs. No inference cost increase (unlike ensembling). Works for CLIP, ALIGN, ViT-G, and NLP tasks (BERT, T5).
what_the_paper_does_not_support: No formal specification (GAP-015). No equivalence checking (GAP-017). No versioning of models (GAP-019). No formal verification (GAP-020). No execution trace. Weight averaging only works when models are in same loss basin — requires same pre-trained initialization. No composition mechanism (just averaging, not selective routing).
paper_core_claims: Averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models (model soup) improves accuracy and robustness
No additional inference cost — averaged model has same architecture as individual model
Greedy soup (sequential addition based on validation accuracy) outperforms uniform averaging
Fine-tuned models from same pre-trained init lie in same loss basin — weight averaging is viable
ViT-G model soup achieves 90.94% on ImageNet (new SotA at time of publication)
Improves out-of-distribution performance and zero-shot transfer

GAP-016.reason: Weight averaging as a form of model compilation: multiple fine-tuned models → single averaged model. But very simple — just element-wise mean.

GAP-017.reason: Weight averaging implies a form of equivalence: models in same basin are 'close enough' to average. But no formal equivalence checking.

GAP-019.reason: Multiple fine-tuned models are combined into a single model — a primitive form of version management. But no registry, no version control.

GAP-020.reason: No formal verification. Empirical accuracy only.

N2_Representation.reason: Weight space as representation: averaging weights in same loss basin. Greedy selection as representation pruning. Loss landscape flatness as predictor of averaging success.

N3_Compiler.reason: Not a compiler. Weight averaging, not compilation.

N4_Artifact.reason: Multiple fine-tuned models as artifacts that can be combined. Model soup itself is a new artifact. Greedy soup selects best subset — primitive artifact selection.

N7_Validator.reason: Validation accuracy as selection criterion for greedy soup. But no formal validation.

N8_ComposerRouter.reason: Greedy soup is a primitive composer: sequentially select models to combine. But composition is just averaging — no routing, no conditional composition, no input-dependent selection.

N9_VersionedRegistry.reason: Multiple fine-tuned models stored and selected from — a primitive model library. But no versioning, no metadata, no formal registry.

limitations_and_failure_boundaries: Weight averaging only works when models are in same loss basin — requires same pre-trained init
Greedy soup depends on validation set — may overfit
No theoretical guarantee that averaging improves performance — empirical observation only
Uniform soup can degrade if models from different basins are included
Only tested on image classification and NLP classification — unclear for generation tasks
No formal analysis of when/why models lie in same basin
strengths_noted: N2 Representation: loss basin / weight space analysis is mathematically interesting
N4 Artifact: multiple models → single combined artifact with no inference cost
N8 ComposerRouter: greedy sequential selection is simple but effective composition
SotA on ImageNet with 25% fewer FLOPs — significant practical impact
Comprehensive evaluation: CLIP, ALIGN, ViT-G, WILDS, NLP tasks
Has become highly influential (weight averaging, model merging)

critical_findings: Identity fully verified: arXiv:2203.05482, Wortsman et al., ICML 2022
N2 Representation: notable — weight space averaging in same loss basin
N8 ComposerRouter: greedy soup as primitive sequential composition
Relevant to Function OS mainly for N2 (representation) and N4 (artifact combination)
